speaker: Narrator
text: The table falls silent. The war, once contained in lines and symbols… no longer stays there.

speaker: Narrator
text: Bataan had been holding for three months. Cut off. Surrounded.

speaker: Narrator
text: What remained of the force was no longer fighting at full strength—it was surviving on what little was left.
*The rustle of paper fades. A chair shifts softly. Footsteps begin—slow, measured.*
*In their place—distant coughing… labored breathing… and the faint, steady sound of dripping water.*

speaker: Narrator
text: Rations had been reduced to a fraction of what a man needed. Rice stretched thin. Canned goods long exhausted.

speaker: Narrator
text: Disease spread faster than reinforcements ever could—malaria, dysentery, and starvation cutting through the ranks.

speaker: Narrator
text: More men were falling in the tents… than on the battlefield.
*Footsteps continue over dirt. Canvas lightly rustles in the wind.*

speaker: Narrator
text: With ammunition nearly gone, food nearly depleted, and tens of thousands too weak to stand—

speaker: Narrator
text: the fight was no longer about holding the line. It was about what remained of the men.
*Footsteps stop. A brief silence. Then—the soft lift of canvas.*
*Coughing becomes clearer. Breathing, closer. A single drop of water falls.*
